MINUTES
  Regular Meeting Notice of the
  Gardena City Council
  Tuesday, July 12, 2022

In order to minimize the spread of the COVID 19 virus, Governor Newsom has signed Assembly
Bill 361. Please be advised that the Council Chambers are closed to the public and that some,
or all, of the Gardena City Council Members may attend this meeting telephonically.

The Regular Meeting Notice and Agenda of the Gardena City Council of the City of Gardena,
California, was called to order at 7:33 PM on Tuesday, July 12, 2022, via Zoom, Mayor Tasha
Cerda presiding.

1.  ROLL CALL

  Present: Mayor Tasha Cerda; Mayor Pro Tem Rodney G. Tanaka; Council Member Mark
  E. Henderson; Council Member Art Kaskanian; and Council Member Paulette C. Francis;
  Other City Officials and Employees present: City Manager Clint Osorio; City Attorney
  Carmen Vasquez; and City Clerk Mina Semenza.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION - None

2.  CLOSED SESSION - None

3.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Michelle Valencia led the Pledge of Allegiance. Michelle is a Recreation Leader I with the
  Recreation & Human Services Team; she just graduated from Lennox Academy and is now
  enrolled at California State University Long Beach where she will be a Political Science
  Major. Michelle works at our parks and in our Summer Day Camp programs. In her spare
  time, she enjoys baking and running.

4.  INVOCATION

  Presented by Mayor Pro Tem Rodney G. Tanaka

5.  PRESENTATIONS

  5.A  ELECTION OFFICIAL'S CERTIFICATION OF OFFICIAL CANVASS OF MUNICIPAL
  ELECTION VOTES
  RESOLUTION NO. 6593, Reciting the Fact of the General Municipal Election held
  on June 7, 2022 Declaring the Results and Such Other Matters as Provided by Law

  RESOLUTION NO. 6593

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  GARDENA, CALIFORNIA, RECITING THE FACT OF THE
  GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION HELD ON JUNE 7, 2022
  DECLARING THE RESULT AND SUCH OTHER MATTERS AS
  PROVIDED BY LAW

  1
   City Clerk Mina Semenza presented the Staff Report.

  It was moved by Council Member Francis, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka,
  and carried by the following roll call vote to Adopt Resolution No. 6593:

  Ayes:  Council Member Francis, Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, Council Members
  Henderson and Kaskanian, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes: None
  Absent: None

5.B  RESOLUTION OF COMMENDATION to the Honorable Art Kaskanian in
  acknowledgment and recognition of Distinguished Service to the City and Community
  of Gardena as a Gardena Council Member

  Mayor Cerda read the Resolution of Commendation and presented it to Mr.
  Kaskanian; a video was also presented. She also thanked and commended Mr.
  Kaskanian for doing an amazing job during these past five years.

  The Honorable Art Kaskanian accepted his Recognition of Distinguished Service.

  Council Member Kaskanian thanked and expressed his appreciation for all his
  supporters, especially his colleagues.

5.C  RESOLUTION OF COMMENDATION to the Honorable Ingrid Tsukiyama in
  acknowledgement and recognition of Distinguished Service to the City and
  Community of Gardena as Gardena's City Treasurer; and, further, to bestow upon
  Her the Title of City Treasurer Emeritus

  Mayor Cerda read the Resolution of Commendation and presented it to Ms.
  Tsukiyama.

  The Honorable Ingrid Tsukiyama accepted her Recognition of Distinguished Service.

  Mayor Cerda thanked Ms. Tsukiyama for her years of service.

5.D  Oath of Office by Newly-Elected / Re-Elected Officials:

  Tasha Cerda  Mayor
  Rodney G. Tanaka  City Council Member
  Wanda Love  City Council Member
  Mina Semenza  City Clerk
  Guy H. Mato  City Treasurer

  Oaths of office were taken by the newly-elected and re-elected officials.

  Mayor Cerda thanked all of her supporters and said she will continue to make the city
  move forward and grow.

  Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka expressed his love and appreciation for everyone that was
  present and all his supporters. He specially thanked his “Gina” for all her support. He
  is looking to give the best four years that he can give and keeping his promises.

  2
   Council Member Love, thanked everyone who supported her and attended her
  swear-in. She promises to continue to be the person that she has been, the person
  you elected and will continue to do what she thinks is best for the city as a whole and
  promises to work as hard as she can on behalf of the residents, businesses, and
  constituents.

  City Clerk Mina Semenza, thanked the community for all their support over the last
  nine years including her family and friends.

  City Treasurer Guy H. Mato thanked and expressed his appreciation to the voters of
  Gardena. He promises to work very diligently and hard for all citizens of Gardena.

  Mayor Tasha Cerda continued the Regular City Council Meeting and noted the
  presence of all the new and continuing Members of the City Council.

  5.E  Boards & Commissions Update - Recreation Commission
  - Chair, Woods Woolwine, Jr., provided the update and video presentation.

  5.F  Certificate of Recognition to the Members of the City of Gardena Explorer Post #142
  for their successes in the 2022 Central Valley Explorer Competition held in Tracy, CA
  - Chief of Police Saffell came into the meeting and recognized his Police
  Explorer Post. Officers Saldana and Nash were present and expressed their
  appreciation and support.

6.  PROCLAMATIONS

  6.A  Parks and Recreation Month - July 2022
  - was proclaimed by Mayor Cerda

7.  APPOINTMENTS – No Appointments were made

8.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  8.A  Waiver of Reading in Full of All Ordinances Listed on This Agenda and that they Be
  read by Title Only
  CONTACT: CITY CLERK

  8.B  Approve Minutes:
  Regular Meeting of the City Council, June 28, 2022
  CONTACT: CITY CLERK

  8.C  Approval of Warrants/Payroll Register, July 12, 2022
  CONTACT: CITY TREASURER

  July 12, 2022: Wire Transfer: 12193-12195; Prepay: 167985 -167988; Check Nos:
  167989 -168154 – for a total Warrants issued in the amount of $2,872,922.04 Total
  Payroll Issued for July 1, 2022: $1,641,332.89.

  8.D  Personnel Report P-2022-13 7-12-22
  CONTACT: HUMAN RESOURCES

  3
   8.E  RESOLUTION NO. 6595, Making the legally required findings to Re-Authorize the
  use of Teleconferencing in accordance with Assembly Bill 361 for meetings of the
  Gardena City Council and other Commissions, Committees and Boards subject to
  State open meeting laws
  CONTACT: CITY MANAGER

  RESOLUTION NO. 6595

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  GARDENA, CALIFORNIA, MAKING THE LEGALLY REQUIRED
  FINDINGS  TO  RE-AUTHORIZE  THE  USE  OF
  TELECONFERENCING IN ACCORDANCE WITH ASSEMBLY BILL
  361 FOR MEETINGS OF THE GARDENA CITY COUNCIL AND
  OTHER COMMISSIONS, COMMITTEES AND BOARDS SUBJECT
  TO STATE OPEN MEETING LAWS

  8.F  Ratify Administrative Approval of the Elderly Nutrition Program Contract ENP202105
  Amendment Ten
  CONTACT: RECREATION AND HUMAN SERVICES

  8.G  Ratify Administrative Approval of the Supportive Services Program Contract
  SSP192003 Amendment Five
  CONTACT: RECREATION AND HUMAN SERVICES

  It was moved by Council Member Francis, seconded by Council Member
  Henderson, and carried by the following roll call vote to Approve all Items on
  the Consent Calendar with the exception of Items 8.F and 8.G:

  Ayes:  Council Members Francis and Henderson, Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka,
  Council Member Love, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes: None
  Absent: None

9.  EXCLUDED CONSENT CALENDAR

  8.F RECREATION AND HUMAN SERVICES - Ratify Administrative Approval of the
  Elderly Nutrition Program Contract ENP202105 Amendment Ten
  - This Item was pulled by Council Member Francis

  Council Member Francis asked if this increase is what we had before; and if it will this
  increase the number of Seniors who can attend the program.

  City Manager Osorio responded to all of her questions.

  8.G RECREATION AND HUMAN SERVICES - Ratify Administrative Approval of the
  Supportive Services Program Contract SSP192003 Amendment Five
  - This Item was pulled by Council Member Francis

  Council Member Francis asked if this is an increase and have, we added any new
  clients; she then asked if the funding is for the entire year and if we can go out and
  request additional funding and recoup an outreach effort or take care of what we
  have now. She also asked about the City’s outreach efforts.

  4
   Council Member Love asked what the increased amount was, and if we got any new
  clients.

  City Manager Osorio responded to all of Council Member Francis and Love’s
  questions.

  It was moved by Council Member Francis, seconded by Council Member Love,
  and carried by the following roll call vote to Approve Items 8.F and 8.G:

  Ayes:  Council Members Francis and Love, Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, Council
  Member Henderson, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes: None
  Absent: None

10. PLANNING & ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY COMMISSION ACTION SHEET

  10.A July 5, 2022 MEETING - Meeting Cancelled

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS – None

11. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES – No Items

12. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT – No Items

13. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - ELECTED & CITY MANAGER'S OFFICES

  13.A COVID-19 Update

  City Manager Osorio presented the update.

  Mayor Cerda and Council Member Love had questions and City Manager Osorio
  replied and answered all their questions.

14. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - PUBLIC WORKS – No Items

15. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - RECREATION & HUMAN SERVICES – No Items

17. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS – TRANSPORTATION – No Items

18. COUNCIL ITEMS

19. COUNCIL DIRECTIVES

  Council Member Henderson

  1. Asked if he can get information from Spectrum regarding our PEC channel and what we
  can do to add content to that channel and see what our agreement consist off.
  Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka seconded it.

  Council Member Love

  1. Asked City Manager Osorio if he can look into getting cell phones for all Council
  Members. Council Member Francis seconded it.
  5
   City Manager Osorio asked for clarification: A request is being made for the City to bring
  an agenda forward to modify and amend the City Council Policy relating to cell phones,
  because currently City Council and Mayor do not receive cell phones or a stipend.
  Council Member Love confirm that the directive was correct.

  Mayor Cerda commented and asked to make an amendment as well.
  Council Member Francis commented and voiced her opinion.

  City Attorney Vasquez advised all members of the City Council that the directive has not
  been agendized and that the item will need to be placed on the agenda for the council
  to discuss and take a vote, whether the council members agreed to have cell phones
  including a staff report that will provide the budgeted amount and cost for council to
  consider at a later meeting.

20. CITY MANAGER REMARKS RE: DIRECTIVES / COUNCIL ITEMS

  City Manager Osorio gave a verbal report of information to follow-up on matters that had
  been directed or requested by the Mayor and Members of Council. Those items were, as
  follows:
  1. Memo regarding the digital message boards at the parks, dated July 5, 2022.
  2. Memo regarding the drought related measures update, dated July 5, 2022.
  3. Memo regarding the Legislative Advocacy update; highlighting the newest earmarks
  that the City of Gardena has received; approximately $4 million for digital equity for
  all; $2 million for the revitalization of Gardena Boulevard; and $1 million in federal
  earmark for Rosecrans Community Center. City Manager Osorio thanked State
  Senator Steven Bradford and Assemblymember Al Muratsuchi for the $6 million and
  Congresswoman Maxine Waters for the $1 million in federal earmark.
  4. Video presentation highlighting the Recreation and Human Services Department
  current and future events:
  • City of Gardena’s 4th of July Park Party, Monday, July 4, 2022, at Rowley Park.
  • Special Lunch for Seniors with Former Dodger Rudy Law.
  • City of Gardena’s Dodger Day, Friday, July 8, 2022.

  Upcoming Events
  • Parks, Recreation, and Human Services Month Celebration! Wednesday, July
  13, 2022; 1:30 p.m. – 3:30 p.m. at the City Hall Lawn.
  • Gardena Police Department invites you to Ice Cream with a Cop on Saturday,
  July 16, 2022, from 11:00 a.m. – 12: 45 p.m., at Rowley Park and then from 1:15
  p.m. to 3:00 p.m. at Arthur Johnson Park.
  • Christmas in July – Candlelight Dinner & Show, Thursday, July 28, 2022, from
  5:00 p.m. – 7:00 p.m., at Nakaoka Community Center Auditorium. Space is
  limited, Pre-Registration is required. For more information contact the Senior
  Bureau at (310)217-9552 or email: seniors@cityofgardena.org or register online
  at www.cityofgardena.org/events.
  • Join the Gardena Police Department for a Night to Unite! Summer Block Party;
  Tuesday, August 2, 2022; 6:30 p.m.-8:30 p.m. on the City Hall Complex.
  • Back-to-School Giveaway – Beginning Saturday, July 16, 2022. Register your
  child at www.cityofgardena.org/events; Supplies limited for grades K-12. Must be
  a resident of the City of Gardena or attend a Gardena COS school to be eligible
  to receive free supplies.

  6
   •  City of Gardena is hosting a Summer UCLA Blood Drive on Thursday, August 11,
  2022; 9:00 a.m. – 2 p.m. at Ruch Gym.
  •  City of Gardena Jazz Festival, Sunday, August 28, 2022, at Rowley Park. Tickets
  On Sale Now! To purchase tickets, visit www.gardenajazzfestival.com/tickets.
  •  Save the Date - Gardena 12th Annual Food, Wine & Brew; Saturday, September
  24, 2022, 12:00 p.m. to 7:00 p.m. at the Gardena City Hall Complex.

  City Manager Osorio thanked Council Member Kaskanian for five years of exemplary
  service and former City Treasurer Ingrid Tsukiyama. He also congratulated Mayor Cerda,
  Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, Council Member Love, and City Clerk Mina Semenza and new
  City Treasurer Guy Mato. He also wished City Attorney Vasquez and Administrative
  Director Ray Beeman a Happy Birthday.

21. COUNCIL REMARKS

  1) COUNCIL MEMBER FRANCIS – Council Member Francis shared some words to the
  family of Jane Hall. She was glad to have had the opportunity to meet Jane Hall, shared
  she was an active participant at the Council Meetings and may she rest in peace. Council
  Member Francis also shared it was a pleasure to serve with Council Member Kaskanian
  and wishes him all the best in the future. Congratulated and Welcomed Council Member
  Wanda Love, Guy Mato, Mina Semenza, Mayor Cerda, and Rodney Tanaka. She is
  looking forward to continuing the great work. Since the last meeting Council Member
  Francis attended the presentation of the new imaging machine at the Memorial Hospital
  of Gardena. She explained it is a state of the art 128 CT scanner that can look into the
  arteries and if anyone needs it, they just need to have a prescription from the doctor to
  get a screening. She also attended the State of the City for Hawthorne and was happy
  to hear the wonderful things that are happening. Lastly, encouraged everyone to stay
  safe and better days are ahead.
  2) MAYOR PRO TEM TANAKA – Since the last meeting, Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka attended
  the City of Torrance 3290 Homeless Center ribbon cutting, he explained they are pallet
  houses by the Courthouse and Police Department. Also attended the LATA grant
  briefing meeting, visited Memorial Hospital to see the new CT scanner with Council
  Member Francis, COGS Homeless Task Force, Dodger Day and commented it was nice
  to see Council Member Kaskanian throw the first pitch, COGS Steering Committee
  meeting, and Hawthorne State of the City as they are celebrating their 100th anniversary.
  Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka shared some words about Jane Hall, Jane Hall was one of his
  biggest supporters and was part of the Rent Mediation Board, she will definitely be
  missed. Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka also thanked Council Member Kaskanian for his five
  years of service, appreciates his dedication and wishes him good luck.
  3) COUNCIL MEMBER LOVE – Council Member Love thanked the community for their
  support and let the Council know that she is looking forward to the next four years
  working together. Council Member Love is excited for what’s ahead and knows it’s going
  to be challenging but believes that they can work together and get it done.
  4) MAYOR CERDA – Since the last Council Meeting Mayor Cerda attended the Gardena
  Memorial Open House for the CT scanner and had the opportunity to present them with
  a certificate. Mayor Cerda also attended the memorial service for the two officers from

  7
   the City of El Monte they were Sergeant Michael Paredes and officer Joseph Santana,
  the Gardena Police Department along with the Honor Guard attended. She attended the
  4th of July celebration at Rowley Park and commented it was one of the best shows they
  have ever had, attended Dodger Day commended Council Member Kaskanian and
  Council Member Henderson for throwing the first pitch, and attended the installation of
  the new officers for the Southern California Inka’s Lions Club for the 2022-2023 new
  members. Lastly, attended a Realtors Event Council of Women’s Forum and was excited
  because her sister is the President of the Southwest Real Estate Board. Mayor Cerda
  shared she will miss Jane Hall she was a dear friend of hers, also shared a few words
  about Jane Hall and her love for Gardena and was a strong advocate for mobile home
  parks. Mayor Cerda shared it was a pleasure serving with Council Member Kaskanian;
  he will be greatly missed and will be a hard act to follow. Congratulated City Attorney
  Vasquez and Director Beeman on their birthdays.
  5) COUNCIL MEMBER HENDERSON – Thanked Council Member Kaskanian for his years
  of service and his dedication and passion and will miss their dialogue on finances and
  the budget, wishes him the best. Congratulated Mayor Cerda, Council Member Love,
  City Clerk Mina Semenza, City Treasurer Guy Mato. Council Member Henderson is
  looking forward to what they will be doing as a group and keep Gardena moving forward.
  Wished City Attorney Vasquez a Happy Birthday. Council Member Henderson shared
  some words about Jane Hall and asked to pray for her family and keep them in our
  prayers. Since the last meeting Council Member Henderson attended the Hawthorne
  State of the City, participated in a panel opportunity to talk about merits and draw backs
  of public private partnerships, South Bay COG Broadband initiative, SCAG meeting, and
  Dodger Day he enjoyed the game with his family. Lastly, expressed Gardena is the city
  of love and they all work together for the betterment of the community as Gardena is the
  jewel of the South Bay.
  Mayor Cerda also shared she also attended the City of Hawthorne State of the City and
  her and Mayor Alex Vargas go way back and the jokes they take on one another is all
  out of fun and love. Mayor Cerda was flattered that they wanted to do their State of the
  City like ours and the thanked all Gardena staff for their work.

22. ANNOUNCEMENT(S)

  Mayor Cerda announced:

  1. Gardena Police Department invites you to Ice Cream with a Cop on Saturday, July 16,
  2022, from 11:00 a.m. – 12: 45 p.m., at Rowley Park and then from 1:15 p.m. to 3:00
  p.m. at Arthur Johnson Park.

23. REMEMBRANCES

  Jane Hall, 93 years of age, beloved Rent Mediation Board Member: Tenant Representative
  since 2002, and a long-time Gardena resident.

  8
   24. ADJOURNMENT

  At 9:56 p.m., Mayor Cerda adjourned the Gardena City Council Meeting to the Closed
  Session portion of the City Council Meeting at 7:00 p.m., and the Regular City Council
  Meeting at 7:30 p.m. on Tuesday, July 26, 2022.

  MINA SEMENZA
  City Clerk of the City of Gardena and
  Ex-officio Clerk of the Council
